title: Equations as Recipes Explained Simply | PUC Chemistry Class 11
description:
A candle under a glass goes out, a rocket carries its own oxygen, and a stove flame quietly uses up the air. So how much oxygen does a flame really need? In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Chemistry (NCERT Chapter 1, Some Basic Concepts of Chemistry) we learn to read a chemical equation like a recipe.

You will see how a chemical equation is written (reactants, products, the arrow and the state symbols g, l, s, aq) and what stoichiometry means. On the molecule bench, methane and oxygen break their bonds and rearrange into carbon dioxide and water, and a live balance counter guides us to CH4 + 2O2 -> CO2 + 2H2O. Then we read it in moles (1 : 2 : 1 : 2), grams (16 g + 64 g -> 44 g + 36 g) and litres at STP (22.7 L : 45.4 L), see why 1 g of methane needs 4 g of oxygen, and meet molarity with the NCERT sodium hydroxide example (0.4 M). A worked example, the exam trap of calculating from an unbalanced equation, an original JEE Main pattern question on propane, a recap card and three questions to check yourself close the lesson.

This is Episode 12 of our PUC Chemistry series.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, NEET and JEE Main students.
